metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7–10 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to catch momentum; increase forecast by 3–8% in the 5–7 day window following sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early horizon (1–3 days) — over-predicts downward moves after recent highs; apply upward bias of 1–3% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to over-smooth transitions; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to adjust forecast volatility — increase if sentiment variance > 0.7, decrease if < 0.3.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period volatility (especially after 15–20 days); add 1–3% upward bias for days 20–30 if sentiment is positive or neutral.
